title: Nested Groups, Block Centring, Letter Units, Two Hands & Real Inputs
description: Five demos: transition groups that keep their clip, wrapperless centring, font-cut units, input-aware buttons, a native dropzone.

drops.title: Groups That Keep Their Clip
drops.description: view-transition-group: contain nests a card's children inside its own group, so the morph can finally be clipped to the card.
drops.concept: Every element with a view-transition-name animates in one flat list of sibling groups, which is why a morphing card's thumbnail and heading sail straight through its corner radius. Setting view-transition-group: contain on the card and nearest on its children nests those groups inside the card's, and ::view-transition-group-children() is the wrapper you can put overflow: clip on. The switch in the panel re-runs the same morph with the children opted out via view-transition-group: none, which is the old flat behaviour side by side.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers — 'Prevent clipping issues (and more) in view transitions by using nested view transition groups'

interaction.mouse: Click a card to morph it open, click again to close
interaction.click: Flip 'nested groups' and reopen to watch the thumbnail escape the radius
interaction.touch: Tap a card; the duration slider stretches the morph out to study it

drops.title: Centred Without a Wrapper
drops.description: align-content applies to plain block containers, so vertical centring stops costing an extra element and a formatting context.
drops.concept: Centring a couple of blocks in a box has meant a flex or grid wrapper for a decade, which quietly switches off margin collapsing and breaks text-overflow on direct children. align-content now works in block layout with the same keywords — start, center, space-between, space-evenly — on the container that already exists. Three panels run the value live, and the 'flex equivalent' switch re-lays them out the old way so the spacing shift is visible rather than theoretical.
drops.source: Trevor Lasn — 'align-content: the simplest way to center content with CSS'

interaction.mouse: Pick an align-content value and drag the height slider
interaction.click: Toggle 'flex equivalent' to compare against the wrapper approach
interaction.touch: Same controls; the panel drops below the demos on narrow screens

drops.title: Units Cut From the Letters
drops.description: cap, ex, ch and ic are measured from the font in use, so an icon sized in 1cap matches the capitals at every size.
drops.concept: Icon-and-label alignment usually ends with a pixel value someone nudged once, at one size, in one family — and it drifts the moment either changes. The font-relative units take their length from the font file itself: cap is cap height, ex is x-height, ch is the advance of 0, ic the advance of 水. A baseline-aligned specimen shows each unit against the glyphs, three label rows compare an icon at 1em, 1ex and 1cap, and a table sets its columns in ch so it reflows with the type.
drops.source: Ahmad Shadeed — 'Better icon and label alignment'
tech: CSS cap / ex / ch / ic / lh units

interaction.mouse: Drag the font-size slider — the cap-sized icon never drifts
interaction.click: Switch family between serif, system and mono to watch the ratios change
interaction.touch: Slider and family chips both work by touch

drops.title: Two Hands, Two Buttons
drops.description: any-hover and any-pointer let one component ship a magnetic preview for mice and press-and-hold commitment for thumbs.
drops.concept: A mouse can hover, so it can be shown what a destructive control will do before committing to it; a thumb cannot, so the commitment itself has to become deliberate. Querying any-hover and any-pointer rather than guessing from viewport width gives each input its own interaction: a sheen that tracks the cursor plus a single click, or a hold that fills the button before it fires. A live read-out prints what the device actually reports, and the branch can be forced either way.
drops.source: MDN — the any-hover and any-pointer media features

interaction.mouse: Hover for the sheen, click once to confirm
interaction.click: Force the touch branch, then press and hold until the fill completes
interaction.touch: Press and hold any card; the hold length is tunable in the panel

drops.title: A Dropzone Around the Real Input
drops.description: ::file-selector-button restyles the browser's own upload button, so drag, paste and preview can wrap a control that still focuses.
drops.concept: The standard upload component hides input[type=file] behind opacity: 0 and puts a label in front of it, which costs the focus ring, the announcement and often the keyboard entirely. ::file-selector-button styles the native button in place instead. Around it sit drag-and-drop, clipboard paste, object-URL previews and a real FNV-1a hash read off the first 512 KB with progress — three variants, no network calls, nothing leaving the page.

interaction.mouse: Drag files onto the zone, or use the restyled native button
interaction.click: Ctrl/⌘+V pastes a file from the clipboard; × removes one from the queue
interaction.touch: The native picker opens on tap; the avatar variant takes one image
